intro: The '$54k technician' figure that circulates in coverage is real but describes only the entry-level title. A data center campus and its supporting operations employ a spectrum of roles, from technicians through licensed engineers, network and security specialists, and senior architects. Government wage data (BLS) is the most reliable benchmark; aggregator and total-compensation figures are self-reported and labeled as such.

roles.role: Senior / staff / principal engineer at hyperscalers

onSiteNote: Where the roles sit matters for local expectations: technicians, facilities engineers, and security staff work at every campus; SOC/NOC teams and licensed engineers concentrate at larger campuses; architect and principal-level roles cluster at corporate and regional hub offices, which some data center regions (like Northern Virginia) also attract. Total compensation figures above $300k reflect equity-heavy packages at major tech employers, not typical pay at a standalone campus.

staffing.title: Why 24/7/365 operation changes the headcount math
staffing.body: Data centers run around the clock, and staffed sites keep people on site at all hours: Uptime Institute guidance calls for at least 1-2 qualified operators on site 24x7x365 at Tier III/IV facilities, and critical-environment technicians, network operations, and security are typical round-the-clock posts. The workforce arithmetic is well established: one continuously staffed seat consumes about 4.2 FTEs at the theoretical minimum (168 hours a week divided by 40) and roughly 4.8-5.4 FTEs once vacation, sick leave, and training are covered. Two things follow. First, published per-facility employment figures (such as JLARC's ~50 workers per typical facility) are total headcount across all shifts, so they should not be multiplied by a shift ratio. Second, that same arithmetic means a '50-person' facility supports only about 9-12 concurrently staffed 24/7 seats, and large multi-building campuses that run on-site network and security operations centers carry headcounts in the hundreds. Round-the-clock reliability is a major driver of the payroll.
